html:
Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire, the first state to unite most of the Indian subcontinent. He reigned from about 320 to about 298 BCE.

His origins are obscure. Tradition pairs him with the Brahmin adviser Chanakya, or Kautilya, to whom the Arthashastra, a manual of statecraft, is credited. With his help Chandragupta overthrew the Nanda kings of Magadha and took their capital, Pataliputra. He also moved into the Punjab, left unsettled after Alexander's retreat.

About 305 BCE he fought Seleucus I, Alexander's successor in the east. The peace gave Chandragupta the lands up to today's Afghanistan, in return for 500 war elephants, and a marriage alliance followed. Seleucus sent the envoy Megasthenes to his court.

Jain tradition says that at the end of his life he gave up the throne, became a monk under the teacher Bhadrabahu and fasted to death at Shravanabelagola in the south. His son Bindusara and grandson Ashoka extended the empire further.
